summary: Task 6 implementation is minimal, correct, and exactly mirrors what the spec asked for. Three deploy files each gained one line (`"t_hunted_source.py"`) in the same grouped position right after `"orangetrack_source.py"`, with byte-for-byte symmetry verified across deploy.sh / deploy.yml / deploy_test.yml. The new pytest invariant file is 51 LOC, three independent test functions, plain-substring assertions (matching the deliberate non-AST contract), CWD-independent via `pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent`. Risk R7 is now CI-catchable; full suite 981 passed, 2 skipped.

suggestions.suggestion: Three test functions are near-duplicates parameterised only by file path and error-message prefix. Consider collapsing into a single `@pytest.mark.parametrize` test with `(deploy_path, label)` tuples — same 3 reported test IDs, less drift surface when the next source module is added (one new EXPECTED_ENTRY rather than three).
suggestions.benefit: Less duplication when a future source module (lamley/orangetrack/t_hunted-style) repeats the exercise. Pytest IDs stay readable via `ids=`.

suggestions.suggestion: `EXPECTED_ENTRY` and `REPO_ROOT` are module-level constants tied to one specific file name. As more new source modules land, this invariant test will accumulate per-file constants. Consider promoting to a list of modules-to-check (e.g. `DEPLOYED_MODULES = [...]`) sourced from a single place — but only if Wave 2/3 introduces more invariant entries; YAGNI applies if this remains a one-off.
suggestions.benefit: Single edit point for the next source-module addition; aligns with the test's own docstring claim that it's an invariant for 'every new first-party module imported by news_bot.py'.
